p1: [low, ominous] In nineteen hundred, three lighthouse keepers vanished... [whispers] and one of them left his coat behind.
[low] On December fifteenth, a passing ship saw the lighthouse was dark.
[low] Eleven days later, the relief boat arrived. [low, tense] Nobody was waiting.
[low] Relief keeper Joseph Moore climbed up alone. [low, tense] Gate shut. Door shut.
[whispers] Inside... nobody. [low] Their beds were empty.
[low] Two sets of oilskins were gone. [low, ominous] The third man's coat... was still hanging there.
[low] In December... in the North Atlantic... [whispers] he went out in his shirt sleeves.
[low] At the west landing, a one-ton stone had been moved... [low, ominous] and a life buoy was torn away, a hundred and ten feet above the sea.
[low] Officially: a huge wave swept all three men away.
[low, tense] But why did the third man go out without his coat? [whispers] What did he see?
[low] That creepy logbook online? Fake. Written decades later.
[low, ominous] Their bodies... [whispers] were never found.
